content_sections.body: Use this lesson language to communicate a simple real-life meaning: Use have and has in simple statements. Model: “Tuan has one brother, and I have two sisters.” Notice the important words and the word order. Mẹo tiếng Việt: hãy hiểu ý của cả câu trước, rồi nói theo cụm ngắn; không cần dịch từng từ.
content_sections.title: Form and meaning

content_sections.body: Read this short situation. A learner needs to use have and has clearly and politely. One useful response is: “Tuan has one brother, and I have two sisters.” Say the model once, then change one safe detail such as a name, place, time, colour, or item when the meaning allows.
content_sections.title: Guided context

content_sections.body: Practise for meaning, not only for memory. Imagine one everyday situation where have and has is useful. First use the model, then make one small change. Check: Is the message clear? Is the target language in the right place? Can another person answer you?
content_sections.title: Use it

exercises.prompt: Read the short message and answer the question about have and has.

questions.question: How many brothers does Tuan have?

exercises.stimulus: Tuan has one brother, and I have two sisters.

exercises.prompt: Put these two parts in a natural order to make a message about have and has.
Make a short, personal response about have and has. Use the lesson language and add one detail that is yours.

criteria: The response communicates a clear meaning about have and has.
The response uses the allocated language in an understandable form.
The response adds an appropriate personal or invented detail.

language_focus: Use have and has in simple statements.
objectives: Use have and has in simple statements.
Use possessions and relationships in one short, clear everyday exchange.

constraints: Do not reveal the transcript before the learner answers.
Ask exactly one comprehension question before showing the transcript.
Use only the supplied project-authored transcript.
listening.goal: Understand one clear detail in a short exchange about have and has.
listening.instruction: Listen once without reading to a short exchange about have and has. Answer the question, then ask to see the transcript and listen again.
listening.question: What animal does the speaker have?
listening.transcript: My family has a small dog. I have a cat.

constraints: Assess pronunciation only when learner audio is available.
Return NOT_ASSESSED when no audio is supplied.
Give one observable sound, stress, or rhythm point rather than general pronunciation advice.
pronunciation.goal: Produce the identified sound, stress, or rhythm feature clearly in a useful phrase.
pronunciation.instruction: Read the concrete sound target aloud: Pronounce has with /z/ and have with /v/. Then read one lesson sentence slowly and once at normal speed.
pronunciation.target: Pronounce has with /z/ and have with /v/.

constraints: Give the tutor one role and the learner one role before the first turn.
Create an information gap: the tutor asks for one missing personal or practical detail.
Use no more than three tutor turns and give one correction only if it blocks meaning.
Finish after the learner has used the target and responded to one follow-up.
speaking.goal: Complete a short, understandable exchange about have and has.
speaking.instruction: Roleplay: you are a learner using have and has; the tutor is a helpful conversation partner. Scenario: you need to use this language in a short everyday interaction. Tutor opening: “Hello. Can we practise have and has?” Reply naturally, ask or answer one follow-up question, and finish the exchange politely. Useful model: Tuan has one brother, and I have two sisters.

constraints: Wait for the learner draft before feedback.
Give at most two brief improvement points about meaning, word order, or target use.
Do not replace the learner draft with a complete rewritten answer.
writing.goal: Produce a short A1 message about have and has with a clear meaning.
writing.instruction: Write 2–3 short sentences for a real-life situation about have and has. Include one sentence pattern from this lesson, then add one true or invented detail. Do not copy this model exactly: Tuan has one brother, and I have two sisters. Submit your draft first.
